# Date gating from the changelog

<!-- Generated by `./gradlew :codex:lore --args=gate`. Do not edit; DateGateReportTest fails when this
     page and a fresh run disagree. -->

Story 7.9 ([ADR-0021](../adr/0021-lore-claim-format.md), amendment). `DateGate` checks a claim's date and the
version it names against when the thing it describes changed, using `codex/v4.0.2/changelog.json` and the release table `lore/release-dates.json`. It flags and never changes a Tier: a Tier
changes by a person or by a citation.

## The finding

The first deliverable of the story is what the changelog can and cannot say.

| What | Count |
|---|---:|
| Entries in `changelog.json`, in 14 changelist classes | 195 |
| Entries that carry a calendar date in their own text | 0 |
| Headings | 593 |
| Headings that state a date (the game's "Released ..." line), in 54 entries | 61 |
| Entries under a class whose name gives a version (`v0_1_X` to `v4_X`) | 194 |
| Entries under `Pixel_Dungeon_Changes` (the vanilla history: dated, no version) | 1 |
| Entries that belong to a release the changelog labels (`v3.3`, `v0.4.3`) | 188 |
| Entries that belong to no release (`Coming Soon`, the vanilla history, the `v0.x.X` banners) | 2 |
| Releases the changelog labels | 55 |
| Releases with a date, and so a row in the table | 53 |
| Headings whose title names an item or mob of the vocabulary, in 55 entries | 92 |
| Headings whose title or text names an item or mob of the vocabulary, in 145 entries | 353 |

The game never dates an entry in its own text: every date it states is in a heading, and what it dates is a
release. So the gate works by release first. A mechanic has no name in the vocabulary (ADR-0022: the vanilla
tree has no mechanics table to diff against), so a claim about a mechanic cannot be tied to a heading and
is gated on its version alone; all 144 claims here are about mobs and items.

A subject is tied to a heading by word, in the heading's title or the text it shows, using the subject, the
vocabulary's names for the subject's class and the class's own name. The text of a heading is read from
the changelist file the heading cites, so a heading titled "Buffs" that says "Goo's pump-up" counts.
A word shared with ordinary prose ("gold", "dart") matches there too; a false tie costs a flag a person
reads, and a missed one costs a stale claim passing, which is why the match errs toward the first.

## The release table

`lore/release-dates.json` has one row per dated release, oldest first: the version, the date in ISO form, the
date as the game words it, and the `path:line` of the changelist line that states it at `v4.0.2`. The game's own changelog is the release notes, kept in the repository, and no date is
typed from memory: `ReleaseDatesTest` derives the rows from the changelog and fails when the file and the
derivation differ, resolves every source, and rejects a row with none.

53 rows, v0.1.0 (2014-08-05) to v4.0 (2026-09-09). Labelled in the changelog and not in the table because the game gives them no date: `v4.0.2`, `v4.0.1`. A claim dated after `v4.0` is therefore flagged for a change in either, since neither can be shown to precede it.

## Does the gate flag nothing, or everything

The 144 claims carry almost no version, so their own verdicts cannot show it. The same gate, run with every
claim given the same anchor, can. The expectations were written in the story file before the first run.

| Every claim anchored at | changed-since | clean | no-entry |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1.0 | 126 | 0 | 18 |
| v3.3 | 15 | 111 | 18 |
| v4.0.2 | 0 | 126 | 18 |

## The 144 claims under `lore/`

| Verdict | Claims |
|---|---:|
| `undated` | 142 |
| `changed-since` | 1 |
| `clean` | 1 |
| `no-entry` | 0 |

Flagged: 143 (`undated` 142, `changed-since` 1). Unflagged: 1 (`clean` 1, `no-entry` 0).

2 claims carry a version or a date the gate can use; every other claim names no version, or only an unusable one ("not stated", "old wiki page", "unspecified"), and has no date. 126 of 144 have at least one heading that names their subject, so the changelog could say something about them if they were dated.

A flagged claim with no code citation is capped at Tier 3 until a person or a citation says otherwise: 4 claims here are in that case, and 0 of them carry a Tier above 3 (that is the number the gate exists to hold at zero, and what holds it is that LoreCheck already refuses a Tier 1 or 2 with no code citation).

Ranked: a claim with a known later change first, then by Tier (a claim the Brain could lean on before one it
could not), then by how many later headings name its subject, then by how many headings name it at all. For an

## What this does not show

- A flag says a claim could not be shown current by its date, not that it is wrong. Some claims are already
  `needs-review` for a different reason (a cited line moved), and the two sets are not the same.
- The tie between a subject and a heading is a word match. It cannot tell a heading that changes the subject
  from one that only mentions it.
- A forum or wiki claim states its date or version rarely; the gate cannot invent one, and the retrieval date is only
  an upper bound on when a claim was written, so it is not used.
- Vanilla Pixel Dungeon claims are not gated: the vanilla history in the changelog has dates and no versions.
